# onlinefdr.com.au

> Accredited online Family Dispute Resolution (FDR) for separating families across Australia. Plain-language, statute-accurate guidance on parenting arrangements, property settlement, spousal maintenance, and Section 60I certificates under the Family Law Act 1975. The practice runs confidential shuttle mediation online and issues Section 60I certificates for parenting matters.

## Core pages
- [What is FDR?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/what-is-fdr/): What Family Dispute Resolution is and how it works under the Family Law Act 1975.
- [How it works](https://onlinefdr.com.au/how-it-works/): The online FDR process step by step, from discovery call to certificate.
- [Parenting](https://onlinefdr.com.au/parenting/): Parenting Plans, Consent Orders, and the best-interests framework after the 2024 reforms.
- [Financial settlement](https://onlinefdr.com.au/financial-settlement/): How property, superannuation, and debt are divided after separation.
- [Section 60I certificates](https://onlinefdr.com.au/section-60i/): What a Section 60I certificate is, who issues it, and when a parenting application needs one.
- [Pricing](https://onlinefdr.com.au/pricing/): Fixed-price packages, agreed up front, with no nasty surprises.
- [FAQ](https://onlinefdr.com.au/faq/): Plain answers to common questions about FDR, parenting, and financial matters.
- [Book a discovery call](https://onlinefdr.com.au/book/): Book a free 15-minute discovery call to check whether FDR is the right path.

## Blog

- [Do de facto couples split property the same as married couples?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/de-facto-property-settlement-australia/): De facto couples divide property under the same law as married couples, but must first prove the relationship and clear the section 90SB gate. No automatic 50/50.
- [How much does a divorce cost in Australia?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/how-much-does-a-divorce-cost-australia/): A divorce costs about $1,100 to file in Australia. The real money is in property and parenting, where your path can swing it by tens of thousands.
- [Do grandparents have a right to see their grandchildren in Australia?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/grandparents-rights-see-grandchildren-australia/): Grandparents have no automatic right to see grandchildren in Australia, but they can apply for a parenting order, and usually must try mediation first.
- [Can you change final parenting orders in Australia?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/can-you-change-final-parenting-orders-australia/): Final parenting orders can be changed by agreement anytime, or through a court only if there's been a significant change of circumstances since they were made.
- [Can you get spousal maintenance after separating in Australia?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/spousal-maintenance-after-separation-australia/): Spousal maintenance is Australia's version of alimony: support for a former partner who cannot yet support themselves. Who qualifies and how it works.
- [Is technology-facilitated abuse a form of family violence in Australia?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/technology-facilitated-abuse-family-violence-australia/): Technology-facilitated abuse, such as tracking and monitoring, is a recognised form of family violence under Australian law. What it is and where to get help.
- [Does family violence affect a property settlement in Australia?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/family-violence-property-settlement-australia/): How the 2025 family law changes make the effect of family violence a required consideration in an Australian property settlement, and how it works in mediation.
- [If your ex breaks a parenting order, do you have to go back to mediation first?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/ex-breaks-parenting-order-mediation-australia/): If your ex breaks a parenting order, you usually must attempt Family Dispute Resolution first, unless a recent serious breach meets a section 60I exemption.
- [Can the court still add back money your ex spent in a property settlement?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/add-backs-property-settlement-australia/): Add-backs largely ended on 10 June 2025. Under section 79(3) the court divides only property that still exists, and Shinohara 2025 confirmed it.
- [Can a parent take a child interstate or overseas without the other parent's consent?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/can-parent-take-child-interstate-overseas-without-consent/): Moving a child interstate is not automatically banned in Australia, but taking a child overseas can be a criminal offence where parenting orders apply.
- [Can you be separated while living in the same house?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/separated-living-same-house-australia/): Yes, you can be separated while living in the same house in Australia, but you need proof the relationship was genuinely over, including two affidavits for divorce.
- [How long after separating can you get divorced in Australia?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/how-long-separated-before-divorce-australia/): You must be separated at least 12 months before applying for divorce in Australia. The extra hurdles for short marriages were removed on 10 June 2025.
- [Can you do family dispute resolution if English is not your first language?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/family-dispute-resolution-in-your-language-australia/): Yes. Online family dispute resolution can be run in your own language using live AI translated captions in Google Meet, which now support 69 languages.
- [How "best interests of the child" actually works after the 2024 amendments](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/best-interests-of-the-child-section-60cc-2024-amendments/): Section 60CC of the Family Law Act was rewritten on 6 May 2024. Here is how the new six-factor best-interests test actually works in 2026, factor by factor.
- [What is the duty of disclosure in financial settlement, and how does it work after the 2024 amendments?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/duty-of-disclosure-financial-settlement-australia/): The duty of full and frank financial disclosure now sits in sections 71B, 90RI, and 90YJA of the Family Law Act 1975. Statutory anchors and case law.
- [Section 60I certificate vs Genuine Steps Certificate: what each is and when you need which](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/section-60i-certificate-vs-genuine-steps-certificate/): A Section 60I certificate is FDRP-issued for parenting only; a Genuine Steps Certificate is party-signed for every application. Statutory anchors explained.
- [At what age can a child decide which parent to live with in Australia?](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/at-what-age-can-child-decide-which-parent-live-with-australia/): There is no age in Australian family law at which a child can decide which parent to live with. What Section 60CC and the High Court of Australia actually say.
- [What 'genuine effort' means in Family Dispute Resolution](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/genuine-effort-family-dispute-resolution/): What genuine effort means in Family Dispute Resolution, what counts and what does not, and how the certificate type can affect later court proceedings.
- [Who keeps the family pet after separation? Companion animals under the 2024 reforms](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/who-keeps-family-pet-separation-companion-animals/): What the Family Law Amendment Act 2024 changed about pets after separation in Australia. Companion animal status, factors the court considers, and shared care.
- [When your child says they don't want to go to the other parent's house](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/child-says-does-not-want-go-other-parents-house/): What Australian family law says when a child resists time with the other parent. How children's views are weighed, and what parents should do next.
- [How superannuation splitting works after separation in Australia](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/superannuation-splitting-after-separation-australia/): Learn how superannuation splitting works in Australian family law property settlements, including the 4-step process, Consent Orders, and duty of disclosure.
- [How the 2026 budget CGT changes impact your property settlement](https://onlinefdr.com.au/blog/budget-cgt-changes-property-settlement/): Understand how the 2026 Federal Budget CGT and negative gearing changes affect Australian family law property settlements and trust distributions.
